headline: Earnings surge on shrinking investment losses

kpis.label: Net earnings attributable to Berkshire shareholders

summary_short: Berkshire's net earnings jumped 119.6% y/y to $10.11B in Q1 2026 as investment mark-to-market losses narrowed to -$1.24B from -$5.04B a year earlier; revenue rose 4.4% to $93.68B and insurance underwriting profit rose 28.5% on the absence of Q1 catastrophe losses.
summary_long: Segment results were broadly higher: insurance underwriting earned $1.72B (+28.5% y/y) with no repeat of Q1 2025's $860M catastrophe losses; BNSF earned $1.38B (+13.4%) on higher revenue and efficiency; Berkshire Hathaway Energy earned $1.11B (+1.5%); manufacturing/service/retailing earned $3.20B (+4.5%, mixed by unit). GEICO's loss ratio rose 4.9pp to 73.9% on higher claims frequency and severity. Net earnings of $10.11B (+119.6% y/y) were driven mainly by investment losses narrowing to -$1.24B from -$5.04B, which management calls 'often meaningless' for assessing performance. Share buybacks were minimal at $234M, all in March. Shareholders' equity rose to $727.18B (+1.4% q/q). No forward guidance was given. Q1 2026 fully consolidates the January 2 OxyChem acquisition.

drivers.explanation: Segment earnings were broadly higher: insurance underwriting $1.72B (+28.5% y/y, no Q1 cat losses vs $860M in Q1 2025), BNSF $1.38B (+13.4%) on higher revenue and efficiency, manufacturing/service/retailing $3.20B (+4.5%, mixed by unit).

drivers.metric: Net earnings attributable to Berkshire shareholders
drivers.explanation: Investment losses narrowed to -$1.24B from -$5.04B a year earlier (equity mark-to-market); management calls these swings 'often meaningless' for assessing performance. 'Other' earnings rose on $249M FX gains (vs -$713M) and higher investment income.
Same investment-loss narrowing as net earnings, plus insurance underwriting and BNSF gains; no repeat of the $1.1B Southern California wildfire catastrophe loss booked in Q1 2025.
Derived from net income +119.6% y/y against revenue +4.4% y/y — the expansion is arithmetic, driven almost entirely by the investment-loss narrowing rather than core operating margin improvement.
Retained earnings accumulation; buybacks were minimal ($234M, all in March, per the Item 2 repurchase table) so had little offsetting effect on equity growth.
